note: Paper test of POSTING resting orders on Kalshi game-winner contracts instead of taking prices (research: reports/NFL and college betting edges.md, rank 2: maker fee 0.0175*p*(1-p) vs taker 0.07*p*(1-p); on Kalshi makers lost far less than takers; exchanges don't limit winners). Simulated, nothing is posted. Each hourly run posts one hypothetical 1-contract YES bid per team at (Pinnacle Shin fair - margin), only when that bid would be the new best bid and below the best ask (a maker, not a taker). The order lives until the next run or 30 min before kickoff. Fill = a trade in that window printed strictly BELOW our bid (the price traded through us, so a resting order there was certainly filled); 'touch' fills (trade at our price) are logged but not graded, since queue position is unknown. The real risk is adverse selection: we get filled when the price is moving against us. Graded by CLV vs Pinnacle's Shin close and by results. ARIZONA: Kalshi's legal status in Arizona is unresolved (state criminal case vs Kalshi, Ninth Circuit ruling Aug 2026): paper only. Do not edit to fit results; bump the version.

version_history.post_rule: only when (fair - margin) would be the new best bid

version_2_note: Changed before any order was ever posted or filled: in the first live runs (12 NFL and 113 college markets matched) v1 posted nothing, because Kalshi's best bid usually sits within 1-2 cents of the sharp fair price, so a bid at fair - 3 cents is never the best bid. v2 joins the queue: post whenever the bid is below the best ask (a maker order), even if other bids are higher. Fill rule unchanged and conservative: counted only when a trade prints strictly below our price, which means every bid at our price was filled. Series fixed: college games are KXNCAAFGAME (found in the first run).
